summary: Gil Fronsdal is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from Stanford University (~1989–1998). He studied under teachers including Jan Nattier, Carl Bielefeldt, Jack Kornfield, and Mel Weitsman, and held posts at the Sati Center and Insight Meditation Center.

Gilles Tarabout works in Indology and religious studies, having studied under Madeleine Biardeau. Attested in 2004, he served as a senior fellow at the CNRS, a member of EHESS, and exchange program director at the Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme.

Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2008) under the doctoral supervision of Jing Yin, having also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

Philosopher Giovanni Gentile studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa and the universities of Florence and Pisa. He held professorships at Palermo, Pisa, and Rome (1917–1944), and served as president of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East.

Sinologist and historian Giovanni Vacca studied at the universities of Genoa and Florence. He taught Chinese at the University of Florence (1910) before holding positions in East Asian languages, history, and geography at Sapienza University of Rome (1911–1948).

Giovanni Verardi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology who studied at Allahabad, Banaras Hindu, and Gorakhpur universities. His career includes positions at Ca' Foscari, the University of Bologna, and a professorship at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1988–1993).

Girindrasekhar Bose studied at Presidency University, Medical College Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He served as Professor of Experimental Psychology at the University of Calcutta (1917–1949) and as president of the Indian Psychoanalytic Society (1922–1953).

Gisela Emma Full, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, studied at the universities of Würzburg and Münster. In 2013, she held research fellow appointments at European University Viadrina and the Samueli Institute.

Prehistorian Gisela Freund studied at the philosophy faculty of the German University of Prague (~1939–1944). She later served as Head of the Department of Prehistory at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1969–1987).

Gisho Nakano, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and obtained a doctorate from Kyushu University. He served as professor and president at Koyasan University and taught at Peking University.
Giti Dutt is an archaeology and interdisciplinary scholar who is attested in 2026 as a PhD student at the Australian National University under the supervision of Assa Doron.
Giuliana Martini is a Buddhist studies scholar who held academic appointments in 2010 at Kyoto University and the Italian School of East Asian Studies.

Giuseppe Bardelli was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Giuseppe Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. He served as a lecturer in Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (~1851–1865).
Giuseppe Mezzofanti studied at the University of Bologna (~1793–1797) and later held an academic post there (~1797–1831), also teaching Giuseppe Bardelli.

Giuseppe Tucci studied at Sapienza University of Rome under Carlo Formichi and Giovanni Vacca, and at Visva-Bharati University. He became a professor at Sapienza (1932) and served as president of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (1947–1978).

Giuseppe Vignato is a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He pursued doctoral studies at Peking University under teachers including Su Bai, Shichang Ma, Chongfeng Li, and Angela Falco Howard, and held a post there (attested 2017).

Buddhist studies scholar Giyu Nishi studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu, Sylvain Lévi, Hakuju Ui, and Taiken Kimura. He served as an assistant at the University of Tokyo (1926) and as a professor at Toyo University (1927).

Glenn H. Mullin is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Ling Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Kalu Rinpoche. He founded the Mystical Arts of Tibet in 1984.
Glenn Wallis is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi and traditional teacher Ross Bolleter, and taught Sonam Kachru.
Gnanawimala Chandima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.
